ei.title: Prior Knowledge as the X-Factor in Reading
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.

questions.passage: The importance of ①<u>what</u> a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension ②<u>testing</u>. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge ③<u>enabled</u> them to outscore readers with far better ④<u>abilities</u>. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①what=관계대명사(정상) ②testing→tested 오류(have+O+p.p.) ③enabled=가능하게 했다(정상) ④abilities=능력(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① what: 'The importance of what a reader brings to the page' — 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 brings의 목적어. of 뒤에 명사절을 이끌며 정상

✅ ② testing: 'had their comprehension testing' — have+목적어+과거분사(p.p.) 사역구문. comprehension은 test의 대상(수동)이므로 tested가 맞음. testing(현재분사/능동)은 오류 ←정답

❌ ③ enabled: 'their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore' — enable+O+to V 5형식. 과거시제 enabled 정상

❌ ④ abilities: 'readers with far better abilities' — 복수 명사 abilities(능력들) 정상
det.tip: have + O + p.p.(사역): had their comprehension tested (이해력을 테스트받았다). 목적어가 동작의 대상이면 과거분사

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students ①<u>who</u> were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was ②<u>composed</u> of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers ③<u>at</u> far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of ④<u>prior</u> knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①who=관계대명사(정상) ②composed=구성된(정상) ③at→with 오류(전치사 선택) ④prior=사전의(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① who: 'students who were asked to read' — 선행사 students(사람)에 관계대명사 who. 정상

❌ ② composed: 'was composed of struggling readers' — be composed of(~으로 구성되다) 수동태. 정상

✅ ③ at: 'outscore readers at far better abilities' — with가 올바른 전치사. 'readers with far better abilities'(훨씬 뛰어난 능력을 가진 독자들). at은 전치사 선택 오류 ←정답

❌ ④ prior: 'the lack of prior knowledge' — 형용사 prior가 knowledge를 수식. 정상
det.tip: readers with better abilities = ~을 가진 독자. with(소유/동반) vs at(장소/시간) 전치사 구분

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess ①<u>that</u> group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge ②<u>deficit</u> about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to ③<u>outscore</u> readers with far better ④<u>abilities</u>. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①that→which 오류(의문형용사 필요) ②deficit=부족(정상) ③outscore=능가하다(정상) ④abilities=능력(정상)
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: 'Guess that group scored higher?' — '어느 그룹이 더 높은 점수를 받았는지 맞혀보라'는 의문에서 의문형용사 which가 필요. that은 의문형용사로 쓸 수 없음 ←정답

❌ ② highlighted: 'is highlighted in a study' — 수동태 과거분사. 정상

❌ ③ made: 'was made up of strong readers' — be made up of(~으로 구성되다). 정상

❌ ④ abilities: 'readers with far better abilities' — 복수 명사 abilities 정상
det.tip: Guess which group = 어떤 그룹인지 맞혀보라. which = 의문형용사(선택). that은 의문형용사 불가

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader ①<u>brings</u> to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were ②<u>knowledgeable</u> about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. ③<u>Have</u> strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, ④<u>was</u> the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①brings=가져오다(정상) ②knowledgeable=해박한(정상) ③Have→Having 오류(동명사 주어 필요) ④was=~이었다(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① brings: 'what a reader brings to the page' — 단수 주어 a reader에 3인칭 단수 현재 brings. 정상

❌ ② knowledgeable: 'struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball' — be 동사 뒤 형용사 보어. 정상

✅ ③ Have: 'Have strong reading skills was not enough' — 주어 자리에 동사원형 Have가 올 수 없음. 동명사 Having이 필요. Having strong reading skills(강한 독해 기술을 가진 것이) = 동명사구 주어 ←정답

❌ ④ was: 'Prior knowledge ... was the x-factor' — 단수 주어 Prior knowledge에 과거 was. 정상
det.tip: 동명사 주어: Having strong reading skills was not enough. Have(동사원형)는 주어 불가 → Having(동명사)

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study ①<u>discussed</u> by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers ②<u>who</u> knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled ③<u>them</u> to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, ④<u>were</u> the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①discussed=논의된(정상) ②who=관계대명사(정상) ③them=목적격(정상) ④were→was 오류(주어 'the lack of prior knowledge' = 단수)
det.analysis:
❌ ① discussed: 'a study discussed by Hirsch' — 과거분사 후치수식. 정상

❌ ② who: 'strong readers who knew little about baseball' — 선행사 readers(사람)에 관계대명사 who. 정상

❌ ③ them: 'enabled them to outscore' — enable+목적격 대명사+to V. 정상

✅ ④ were: 'Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, were the x-factor' — A or B 구조에서 동사는 B(가까운 주어)에 수일치. 'the lack of prior knowledge'는 단수이므로 was가 맞음. were는 오류 ← 정답
det.tip: A or B + 동사: 동사는 B에 수일치. the lack(단수) → was. were는 복수형으로 오류

questions.passage: The ①<u>importance</u> of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were ②<u>knowledgeable</u> about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their ③<u>comprehension</u> tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge ④<u>surplus</u> about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①importance(중요성) ②knowledgeable(해박한) ③comprehension(이해력) ④surplus(잉여←deficit)
det.analysis:
❌ ① importance: 독자가 가져오는 것의 '중요성' → 적절

❌ ② knowledgeable: 야구에 대해 '해박한' 독자 → 적절

❌ ③ comprehension: 각 그룹의 '이해력' 테스트 → 적절

✅ ④ surplus: '잉여'는 지식 '부족(deficit)'이라는 원문과 정반대. 독해력은 강하지만 주제 지식이 부족한 학생에게 기술만으로는 불충분했음 ←정답
det.tip: deficit(부족/결핍) ↔ surplus(잉여/초과). knowledge deficit = 지식 부족

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of ①<u>strong</u> readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge ②<u>discouraged</u> them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the ③<u>lack</u> of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①strong(강한) ②discouraged(단념시켰다←enabled) ③lack(부족) ④x-factor(결정적 요인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① strong: '강한' 독자로 독해력이 뛰어남 → 적절

✅ ② discouraged: '단념시켰다'는 사전 지식이 높은 점수를 '가능하게 해주었다(enabled)'는 원문과 정반대 ←정답

❌ ③ lack: 사전 지식의 '부족' → 적절

❌ ④ x-factor: 사전 지식이 '결정적 요인' → 적절
det.tip: enabled(가능하게 했다) ↔ discouraged(단념시켰다/낙담시켰다)

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is ①<u>highlighted</u> in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of ②<u>talented</u> readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their ③<u>comprehension</u> tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better ④<u>abilities</u>. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①highlighted(강조된) ②talented(재능 있는←strong) ③comprehension(이해력) ④abilities(능력)
det.analysis:
❌ ① highlighted: 연구에서 '강조된' → 적절

✅ ② talented: '재능 있는 독자'는 원문의 'strong readers'와 다른 단어이긴 하지만, 맥락상 '독해력이 강한(strong)' 독자를 '재능 있는(talented)'으로 바꾼 것이 아님. 원문에서 이 그룹은 야구를 모르지만 독해력이 '강한(strong)' 것이 핵심. talented는 strong의 부적절한 대체 ←정답

❌ ③ comprehension: '이해력' 테스트 → 적절

❌ ④ abilities: '훨씬 뛰어난 능력' → 적절
det.tip: strong(독해력이 강한) ↔ talented(재능 있는): 원문은 strong readers이며 talented는 의미가 다름

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of ①<u>strong</u> readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were ②<u>knowledgeable</u> about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far ③<u>inferior</u> abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①strong(강한) ②knowledgeable(해박한) ③inferior(열등한←better) ④x-factor(결정적 요인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① strong: 독해력이 '강한' 독자 → 적절

❌ ② knowledgeable: 야구에 대해 '해박한' → 적절

✅ ③ inferior: '열등한'은 '훨씬 뛰어난(far better)'이라는 원문과 정반대. 사전 지식이 있는 약한 독자가 능가한 대상은 '훨씬 뛰어난 능력'의 독자 ←정답

❌ ④ x-factor: 사전 지식이 '결정적 요인' → 적절
det.tip: far better(훨씬 뛰어난) ↔ inferior(열등한). 능가 대상은 더 뛰어난 독자여야 의미가 성립

Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with __________. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 독해 기술로는 부족한 학생들의 조건: 주제에 대한 지식 부족
det.analysis:
❌ ① a passion for baseball(야구에 대한 열정): 열정이 아니라 지식의 문제

✅ ② a knowledge deficit about the topic(주제에 대한 지식 부족): 독해력은 있지만 야구 지식이 없어서 불충분했다는 원문과 일치 ←정답

❌ ③ an advantage over other students(다른 학생에 대한 이점): 첫 번째 그룹은 오히려 불리했음

❌ ④ a natural talent for reading(독서에 대한 타고난 재능): 독해력은 이미 강했으므로 부적합
det.tip: knowledge deficit about the topic = 주제에 대한 지식 결핍. 독해력 ≠ 이해력

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: x-factor의 정체: 사전 지식(있거나 없거나)
det.analysis:
❌ ① Strong reading skills, or the development of such skills(강한 독해 기술이나 그 개발): 독해 기술은 충분하지 않았다고 했으므로 x-factor가 아님

❌ ② The difficulty of the baseball passage, or the topic itself(야구 지문의 난이도): 지문 난이도가 아니라 독자의 배경지식이 핵심

❌ ③ The teaching method used in the classroom(교실에서 사용된 교수법): 교수법은 본문에 언급 없음

✅ ④ Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge(사전 지식, 또는 우수한 독자의 경우 사전 지식의 부족): 원문과 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: x-factor = prior knowledge (있으면 유리, 없으면 불리)

det.korean: 이 연구에서 강조된 것의 중요성

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit.

(A) Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities.

(B) This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball.

(C) The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers.

det.korean: (B)→(C)→(A) 순서: 연구 소개→그룹 설명→결과 및 시사점
det.analysis:
도입문: 히르쉬의 연구에서 독자가 가져오는 것의 중요성이 강조됨

(B) 'This study' = 도입문의 연구를 지칭. 두 그룹 소개 + 첫 번째 그룹 설명 → 도입 직후

(C) 'The second group' = (B)의 첫 번째 그룹에 이어 두 번째 그룹 설명 + 결과 → (B) 직후

(A) 'Having strong reading skills was not enough' = (C)의 결과에 대한 해석 + 사전 지식의 역할 → (C) 직후

✅ ① (B)-(C)-(A) ←정답
det.tip: This study → 첫 그룹 → 둘째 그룹 + 결과 → 해석. 시간/논리 순서

det.analysis:

❌ ② '야구 지식이 있는 약한 독자가 더 높은 점수를 받았다': 'The struggling readers ... scored higher' — 일치

❌ ③ '독해 기술만으로는 높은 이해력에 충분하지 않았다': 'was not enough' — 일치

✅ ④ '사전 지식은 이해력에 별 영향을 미치지 않았다': 'was the x-factor' — 결정적 요인이었으므로 '별 영향 없다'는 정반대 ←정답
